key_insight: EgoExplorer introduces a wearable, multi-modal dataset that captures human loco-manipulation as coordinated vision, motion, and touch events in real-world settings. This gives researchers a more complete view of how people move, stabilize, and interact with objects during tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the lack of scalable, portable datasets that jointly capture locomotion, posture, and object interaction during human demonstrations. Existing datasets often miss one or more of these signals, making it hard to learn humanoid loco-manipulation from realistic in-situ behavior.
method: Built a wearable observatory system for collecting synchronized vision-motion-touch data during human loco-manipulation.
Recorded a 100-hour dataset spanning diverse environments and task contexts to improve realism and coverage.
Focused on capturing the coupled evolution of movement, body posture, and tactile/object interaction as tasks unfold.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset provides richer supervision for training and evaluating humanoid robots and embodied agents in loco-manipulation. It can help improve policies that require coordinated perception, movement, and contact-rich interaction in everyday environments.

paper_title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
paper_authors: Yunsong Zhou, Xuekun Jiang, Haiqi Shen, Hangxu Liu, Chaojian Shi
